subject: Post-call recap: GeneForge air-gapped deployment follow-up
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Mar 2028 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: GeneForge discovery (air-gapped)

Hi team,

Quick post-call recap from my discovery with Dr. Priya Rao / Ops at GeneForge (call at 15:00 UTC): high-level context and immediate asks so we can thread owners and next steps.

Key constraints they repeated several times:
- Fully air-gapped environment: no outbound connectivity from inference cluster. Any telemetry must be exportable via signed bundles only.
- Offline upgrades only: they require signed upgrade bundles and manual install via removable media (USB / internal transfer). No in-place downloads.
- Hardware preference: they prefer H100-class cards; current racked infra will accept 3x 8-GPU nodes initially (want sizing guidance).
- Maintenance windows: monthly planned window, prefer local-night (UTC 02:00-04:00) for minimal user impact. Emergency patches allowed but must be scheduled with 48h notice.
- KMS/HSM: they will manage keys in their on-prem HSM; want to validate our offline key wrapping flow.
- Fallback policy: want the ability to fall back to a Redwood Dedicated capacity during longer upgrade windows, but only for specific models and with strict data residency controls.

Their timeline: procurement approval expected late May; POC requested for June (4-week POC preferred).

Action items I committed to on the call:
1) Ben: produce an initial capacity matrix (per-model throughput/latency for H100 hardware) and a storage/I/O BOM draft.
2) Karthik: draft a 1-page SOW and an offline upgrade process sketch (signed-bundle flow + rollback plan).
3) Me: send them an offline-ops checklist and follow-up clarifying the fallback policy boundary and data processing addendum question.

Attachments: I dropped the offline-ops checklist draft on the call (attached here as a stub) and a starter capacity BOM.

Please flag any items you think we should escalate to solutions/research (e.g., kernel-level offline signing, custom quantization support).

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0134

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Mar 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: GeneForge discovery (air-gapped)

Thanks Naomi — good notes. A couple quick clarifying Qs before I start the capacity matrix:

1) When they say "H100-class," do they mean specifically Nvidia H100 SXM or will PCIe variants be acceptable? That affects our thermals/BOM.
2) Confirm expected concurrency: they said "initially 3 nodes" — do they mean 3x 8-GPU rack servers behind an L4 load balancer, or 3 total physical servers? I want to size batch queues properly.
3) Spare parts & racking: do they expect Redwood to ship on-call spare GPUs / NVMe spares, or will that be an ops handoff to their datacenter partner? If they want spare parts, we should surface lead times in the BOM.

I can start with a conservative H100 SXM assumption and include A100/Hopper PCIe variants as alternatives.

I'll aim to have a first-pass matrix by EOD Thu (23rd).

Ben
Ben Carter | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Priya Rao <priya@geneforge.com>, GeneForge Ops <ops@geneforge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Mar 2028 16:40:00 +00:00
Subject: Follow-up & next steps from today's call (GeneForge / air-gapped)

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the clarity on the air-gapped requirements. Per our call, I summarized the items we discussed and listed a few targeted questions so we can scope a clean POC and delivery path.

Summary (short):
- Requirement: Private, air-gapped private deployment (no outbound connectivity).
- Desired hardware: H100-class inference nodes; initial target capacity: ~3x multi-GPU servers (you indicated this is to justify initial throughput testing).
- Upgrade model: signed upgrade bundles, manual install via removable media.
- Key management: customer-managed HSM, key wrap / unwrap flow must be demonstrable in POC.
- Fallback: acceptable to route traffic to Redwood Dedicated for short windows (we understand this is a sensitive point; we'll define strict controls).

Questions to confirm (please reply inline if possible):
1) Exact hardware form-factor preference: H100 SXM vs PCIe? If uncertain, we can propose both with a cost delta.
2) Concurrency expectations (qps / concurrent requests) for the baseline POC workload.
3) Who will perform physical installs (GeneForge ops vs. a local integrator)? If integrator, please share contact.
4) Are there existing maintenance windows (e.g., 02:00-04:00 UTC monthly) we should default to for the POC?
5) Legal: do you need a Data Processing Addendum or additional contractual language before POC?

Next steps we propose: 
- Ben to share capacity matrix + BOM (target: Thu 23 Mar).
- Karthik to draft SOW + offline upgrade flow (early next week).
- Technical deep dive (remote) to validate HSM flow and key-wrapping: proposed date Apr 5th, 14:00 UTC.

I attached a short offline-ops checklist and a starter capacity BOM for your review. If this looks right, can we lock the Apr 5th slot for a 60–90 minute technical session?

Regards,
Naomi
---
Attachment: geneforge-offline-ops-checklist.pdf (see checklist items for signed bundle steps)

From: Dr. Priya Rao <priya@geneforge.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Cc: GeneForge Ops <ops@geneforge.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 08:35:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & next steps from today's call (GeneForge / air-gapped)

Thanks Naomi — helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side (inline):

> 1) Exact hardware form-factor preference: H100 SXM vs PCIe?
We strongly prefer H100 SXM for performance density; PCIe is acceptable as fallback if lead times are significantly shorter. Please call this out in the BOM.

> 2) Concurrency expectations (qps / concurrent requests) for the baseline POC workload.
For the POC we'd like to validate roughly 120 concurrent users with peak qps ~250 for our internal scoring pipelines. Latency target is 150–250ms p50 for 2k token average prompt — we know we'll adjust for batch sizing.

> 3) Who will perform physical installs?
GeneForge Ops will take primary responsibility for racking; we do have a local integrator for heavy lifts (contact: Marco Silva, marco@rackworks.eu).

> 4) Maintenance windows?
Monthly maintenance window 02:00–04:00 UTC works. Emergency patching must be coordinated, but we can allow a 48h scheduled emergency window.

> 5) Legal: do you need a DPA?
Yes, please include a standard DPA and confirm if you can sign our data processing addendum; we'll share our template if needed.

A couple of asks from our legal/ops teams:
- Please indicate how telemetry will be handled during the POC (we need explicit guarantees that no outbound telemetry leaves the air-gapped network; logs should be exportable as signed bundles only).
- Can you provide a short SOW outline and a one-page fallback policy that limits what can run on Dedicated during maintenance (models allowed, data residency controls)?

We are broadly interested in the fallback option you mentioned (Dedicated for long upgrades) — that is a useful operational lever if it's tightly controlled.

If you can share the capacity matrix and a draft SOW by EOD Thu, we can forward to procurement ahead of their week-of-May review.

Best,
Priya
Dr. Priya Rao | Head of ML Infrastructure, GeneForge Biotech
priya@geneforge.com

Ben/Karthik, please include estimated lead times for spare parts (GPUs / NVMe) and an explicit note on the sealed-bundle verification process we support.

Priya — once Ben's matrix is in, can we lock Apr 5th 14:00 UTC for the deep dive? I will send a calendar invite and include Marco Silva (rackworks) so we can validate physical handoff expectations.

Appreciate the quick turnaround on procurement timing — we'll prioritize the matrix and SOW.

Cheers,
Naomi
